property_summary: For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutated version always returns false.
For any interfaceId, the return value of supportsInterface must equal that of the original AccessControl logic (supporting IAccessControl and IERC165), but the mutant always returns false.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must always return the same boolean in the reference implementation; the mutant breaks this by returning false unconditionally.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true if and only if interfaceId is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant always returns false, violating that for these interface IDs.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the mutant always returns false, violating this for those interfaceIds.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true only if interfaceId is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version always returns true, so it will incorrectly return true for an arbitrary unrecognized interfaceId (e.g., 0x11223344).
The reference supportsInterface returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the buggy version returns false due to negation.

For any input interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true when the input equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId OR super.supportsInterface returns true, while the buggy version negates this condition, returning false for at least one such input.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if either IAccessControl or IERC165 is supported; the mutant negates this, returning false for IAccessControl.

supportsInterface must return true exactly when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or IERC165's supportsInterface returns true; the mutant negates this, returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must equal (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) || c.supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId); the mutant negates the return value, breaking this equivalence.
Contract C correctly supports the IAccessControl interface via its override, whereas the buggy version drops that check and incorrectly returns false for the IAccessControl interface ID.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns the same as interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || super.supportsInterface(interfaceId); the buggy version drops the IAccessControl check, so when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and ERC165.supportsInterface returns false, the bug returns false while reference returns true.

For any bytes4 identifier, supportsInterface returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version drops the IAccessControl check and returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId regardless of ERC165 result, but the buggy version only delegates to super.supportsInterface and thus returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId when super returns false.

For any interface ID, c.supportsInterface() returns the same as (id == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || super.supportsInterface()); the buggy version drops the IAccessControl check, so it returns false when id equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and ERC165 would return false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true when interfaceId is either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId (the latter via super); the bug returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, if the call supportsInterface(interfaceId) in C returns true, then it must also return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant breaks this because it only matches type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, so type(IERC165).interfaceId returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) returns true; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true only if it is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId, violating this inclusive behavior.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface should return true exactly for the supported interfaces; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId, which should be supported via inheritance.
For any role and account, if the role has never been granted, hasRole must return false in the reference, but the buggy version always returns true.

For any non-zero role whose admin role grants it to a second account, after the granted account renounces that role, hasRole must return false for the role and that account in the reference; the bug always returns true.
For any role and account, if the role is revoked by an admin, hasRole must return false in the reference, but the buggy version always returns true.

For any role and account, c.hasRole(role, account) returns true if and only if account was granted that role; the bug version always returns false, so it will differ for any account that actually has the role.
After granting a role to an account, hasRole(role, account) returns true in the correct contract and false in the mutant.

After granting a role to an account, hasRole for that role and account returns true in the reference, but false in the mutant; the rule is: hasRole never returns false for an account that was just granted the role.

In the reference, calling hasRole for any role and account always returns the same boolean as the internal _roles mapping; the mutant always returns false, so there exists some input where they differ.
